paras: The killing of Joe Burnes was the fatal shooting of a Black barber by a police officer in Kansas City, Missouri, reported in a wire dispatch dated January 2, 1882. Officer Lovett, who was said to have mistaken Burnes for a thief, shot him dead when he did not stop, and Lovett was reported exonerated. The item ran as a single paragraph of telegraph news in papers from Texas to Washington.

According to the Kansas City dispatch, Burnes, described as "a negro barber," was taken by Officer Lovett for a thief and ordered to halt. Burnes "refused to stop and was shot dead." The dispatch gave no time of day, no location within the city and no account from Burnes's side, and the explanation that he was mistaken for a thief appears without attribution.
The same dispatch stated that "Lovett has been exonerated," without saying by whom or on what finding. No report of an inquest, local investigation or later proceedings appears in the coverage.

White papers carried the story on January 3, 1882, in identical wording, among columns of brief telegrams. The Savannah Morning News headed it "Shot by a Policeman," the Dallas Daily Herald "Killed by Mistake," and the Richmond Dispatch "Fatal Case of Mistaken Identity." The Knoxville Daily Chronicle, the Washington National Republican and the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer ran the item without a separate heading. The Dallas and Lancaster papers spelled the victim's name "Burns," and the Dallas paper printed the officer's as "Lovette." None of these papers added comment, and all framed the shooting as an accident of mistaken identity rather than questioning the officer's account.

bases: A police officer shot and killed a Black barber he took for a thief when the man did not halt; no crowd was reported (A1, A3, A5).

accounts.label: Kansas City wire report
accounts.gist: Officer Lovett, mistaking Burnes for a thief, ordered him to halt; Burnes refused to stop and was shot dead, and Lovett has been exonerated. The mistaken-thief explanation is given without attribution and appears to rest on the officer's side.

framing.detail: Papers in Savannah, Knoxville, Dallas and Washington ran the identical brief under headings such as 'Shot by a Policeman' and 'Killed by Mistake', with no comment.

conflicts.note: Spelling variants of the same wire text; most papers print 'Burnes' and 'Lovett'.
